title: Stalkwise flat tensor pullback preserves kernels
statement: Let $g:X\to Y$ be a morphism of ringed spaces [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] such that every stalk map $O_{Y,g(x)}\to O_{X,x}$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $P:\operatorname{Mod}(O_Y)\to\operatorname{Mod}(O_X)$ be additive [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with specified object equalities to $O_X\otimes_{g^{-1}O_Y}g^{-1}M$ and map equalities to the inverse-image maps followed by change of rings transported along those equalities [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then for every module-sheaf morphism $a:M\to N$, $P$ preserves the kernel diagram $\operatorname{parallelPair}(a,0)$.

source.place: Tag 02N4, lemma-pullback-flat, kernel part of exactness; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02N4

proof.text: For each point x, form k as the presheaf inverse-image stalk map followed by the stalk of sheafification, and psi as the stalk of the adjoint structure-ring map. On germs, the sheaf adjunction unit is the presheaf unit followed by sheafification. The hom-equivalence identity then gives k followed by psi equal to g.hom.stalkMap x. This is proved directly in Lean using stalk_hom_ext and the adjunction identities.

Apply inverse-image stalk scalar transport and the natural change-of-rings stalk comparison. Compose their isomorphisms to obtain delta M from extension of scalars of the original stalk to the stalk of the tensor pullback. Check naturality on generators 1 tensor m using ExtendScalars.hom_ext, the tensor map formula, and both stated naturality formulas. Transport delta through the given object equalities and map equality hm to obtain a natural isomorphism of functors.

Stalk functors preserve finite limits: compose the sheaf-of-modules forgetful functor with the abelian-sheaf stalk functor and reflect preservation through the module-to-abelian-group forgetful functor. Flat extension of scalars preserves finite limits, by ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat. The preceding natural isomorphism therefore makes P followed by each stalk functor preserve finite limits.

The stalk functors jointly reflect isomorphisms: forget to abelian sheaves, use Presheaf.isIso_of_stalkFunctor_map_iso, and reflect through SheafOfModules.toSheaf. Apply Mathlib JointlyReflectIsomorphisms.jointlyReflectsLimit to the P-image of the chosen limit cone of parallelPair a 0. Each stalk image is limiting by the preceding preservation instance. Finally preservesLimit_of_preserves_limit_cone gives the required preservation. The argument applies also to empty X and zero stalk rings.

lean.statement:
theorem stalkFlat_tensorModulePullback_preservesKernels
    {X Y : RingedSpace.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y)
    (hg : ∀ x : X, (g.hom.stalkMap x).hom.Flat)
    (P : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y) ⥤
      SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X))
    (h : ∀ M, P.obj M = SheafOfModules.changeOfRings.{u, u, u}
      (CochainComplex.tensorPullbackRingMap
        g.hom.base X.sheaf
        Y.sheaf ⟨g.hom.c⟩)
      (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageModule g.hom.base
        Y.sheaf M))
    (hm : ∀ {M N} (a : M ⟶ N),
      P.map a = eqToHom (h M) ≫ SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsHom.{u, u, u}
        (CochainComplex.tensorPullbackRingMap
          g.hom.base X.sheaf
          Y.sheaf ⟨g.hom.c⟩)
        (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageModule g.hom.base
          Y.sheaf M)
        (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageModuleMap g.hom.base
          Y.sheaf M a) ≫ eqToHom (h N).symm)
    [P.Additive] :
    ∀ {M N : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y)} (a : M ⟶ N),
      PreservesLimit (parallelPair a 0) P
